headline: Researchers at QuTech in Delft have built a quantum chip measurement step that removes 98.4 percent of leaked qubit states without slowing the operation.
score_reason: Specific technical result from a university lab, one outlet's write-up, no outside review reported.
importance_line: It targets a main source of errors that standard error correction cannot fix, which matters to quantum hardware builders, though it is a lab result on one type of chip.
summary: Quantum Zeitgeist reports that QuTech at Delft University of Technology added a leakage reduction unit to the way a transmon qubit (a superconducting qubit) is read out, removing 98.4 percent of leakage, where a qubit slips out of its useful states and causes errors. The step adds no time to the measurement, kept 99.2 percent accuracy in reading the qubit and, combined with neural-network decoding, lowered logical error rates in test error-correction runs.
notes: Paper title: Improved error correction with leakage reduction units built into qubit measurement in a superconducting quantum processor; publication date not stated.
